decision: the AI writes a checked manifest, not code
why: a generated script can do anything, a manifest can only do what the runtime allows

decision: use the local claude CLI for the prototype
why: no API key needed for a demo, production swaps to the API

decision: clickable HTML canvas instead of a real Figma file
why: the Figma connector was not connected
evidence: design canvas link in the final reply

decision: check every operation, field and quote against the source with plain code
why: the model must not grade its own work

decision: build a fault mock from the manifest with 29 scenarios
why: real vendors rarely offer a sandbox, and faults cannot be triggered on demand

decision: add a live read-only check after the sandbox
why: a mock built from the manifest cannot prove the manifest matches the vendor
result: live check is required before approval

decision: replaced a depth limit in deref with a node budget
why: Calendly schemas were cut off and the model could not see field names

decision: rescored endpoint ranking and gave usage its own quota
why: person-scoped paths such as /users/{id}/events beat real list endpoints

decision: block a page number used as an offset
why: Zendesk generation would have skipped users without any error

decision: carry GraphQL cursors in variables and read hasNextPage
why: Linear pagination could not be described before

decision: ran a mutation check over the safety code
why: tests that cannot fail prove nothing
result: found 2 real test gaps, both fixed, 2 equivalent mutants removed

decision: scored 11 vendors against a hand-written answer key
why: vendor variety is the real risk, not Calendly alone
result: 10 of 11 strict, 0 sandbox failures, GitHub miss is page_number versus link_header and still works

decision: show Repair with AI only for contract errors
why: a bad token is not a connector bug
result: found in QA with a fake token on real Calendly

decision: ran the full gated flow against public JSONPlaceholder
why: checks the real path from generate to active
evidence: scratchpad e2e run in the transcript
result: skipped gates refused with 409, active with a bound hash

decision: scan the whole spec for injection text, not only the digest sent to the model
why: an adversarial test showed text outside the digest raised no flag

decision: removed bare act as from the injection pattern
why: it matched contact associated and vendor prose such as act as a wildcard in real specs

decision: reran the adversarial test with injection inside the users operation
why: the first run proved little because that text never reached the model

decision: fixed all 12 findings from an independent security review, each with a regression test
why: 54 tests had missed them, including code injection, host spoofing, IPv6 SSRF and truncated walks reported complete

decision: split the reconcile verdict into absent users and inactive users
why: a license reclaim needs activity data, removing a user does not

decision: recommend Sonnet 5.5 through the API
why: Opus and Haiku both picked a wrong GitHub endpoint, Haiku was blocked on Zendesk, and a wrong endpoint passes the sandbox
result: 3 vendors, one run each, small sample

decision: reran 11 vendors on the hardened code with Sonnet
why: checks the security fixes did not break real vendors
result: 10 of 11 strict, 0 sandbox failures, $1.256 total, median $0.105, median 24s, max 79s

decision: traced the Calendly retries to an unset template value
why: a jump to 3 attempts could have been a regression from the fixes
evidence: one rerun printing each attempt's findings
result: unbound_template blocked it and repair fixed it, not a regression

decision: reran the full gated flow on public JSONPlaceholder on the hardened code
why: the earlier run predated the fixes
result: skipped gates 409, sandbox 21 pass 0 fail, live 10 users 2 pages, masked emails, approval needs name and ack, active then quarantined

decision: raised phone tap targets to 44px and input text to 16px
why: the phone check found undersized controls, and smaller input text zooms the page on iOS
result: no horizontal scroll, no undersized controls
